title: ZTF data show no common brightening of 10 classical nova progenitors in the final year before eruption, and no precursor alert in the final 30 days of 22 novae (2018-2026)
abstract: Old photographic records show a pre-eruption rise in 2 of 22 novae (Collazzi et al. 2009). We tested this with ZTF data for the 63 Galactic novae in Koji Mukai's list that were discovered from 2018-06 to 2026-10 at declination above -31 degrees. In ZTF DR24 PSF light curves (to 2025-10), the same ZTF object that shows the eruption gives the progenitor light curve for 14 novae. Ten classical novae have enough data. The final-year median minus the earlier median has a median of +0.007 mag. Relative to neighbour stars of similar brightness at the same epoch, the median is -0.002 mag (95% interval -0.051 to +0.017 mag). No progenitor changed by 0.5 mag or more (0 of 10; 95% upper limit 31%). Thus our data cannot reject the Collazzi rate. V1674 Her became brighter by about 0.47 mag (g) over 4 years, at a slope steeper than all 20 neighbour stars, but mostly 2 to 3 years before eruption. Its ZTF object can contain light from a neighbour star. V6598 Sgr became brighter by about 0.3 mag over 3 years. V6596 Sgr was 0.2 to 0.4 mag fainter in its final observed season. In the ZTF public alert stream (ALeRCE), 22 novae with quiet progenitors had 260 covered nights in the 30 days before eruption (median 5-sigma limit 20.0 mag), and none gave a precursor alert. Two flagged detections were the start of the eruption. ZTF saw 3 eruptions 2.8 to 24.5 days before their catalogue discovery. Main limitations: the sample is small, the progenitors are faint and can be blended, DR24 ends before the 2026 eruptions, and seasonal gaps remove the final months of some bulge novae.

display.caption: ZTF DR24 nightly PSF magnitudes of the progenitors (one filter per nova) against years before the eruption onset. The dashed line is the median before the final year. The shaded band is the final year, and the orange line is its median. D1 is the difference. Plots marked blend? use a ZTF object 1.0 to 1.6 arcsec from the nova position.

Final-year shift D1 of each progenitor (blue; orange = recurrent nova U Sco) and of neighbour stars of similar brightness on the same CCD quadrant at the same epoch (gray). Negative values mean brighter before eruption. Only V1674 Her (brighter) and V6596 Sgr (fainter) are outside most neighbours.

ZTF public alert history (ALeRCE) in the 30 days before t_ref, the earlier of the first eruption alert and the catalogue discovery. Gray triangles are nights with no alert (5-sigma limits near 20 mag). Orange points are positive alerts; they occur only for progenitors that were already variable (marked *). Blue diamonds mark the first eruption alert, and black bars mark the catalogue discovery.

citations.reason: Collazzi et al. 2009: pre-eruption light curves of 22 novae from photographic plates, with 2 real rises. We test the claim with ZTF CCD data and find no rise of 0.5 mag in 10 novae; this agrees with their low rate but cannot reject it.
Schaefer 2010: photometric histories of Galactic recurrent novae, with no pre-eruption rises.
ZTF data system and PSF light curves (Masci et al. 2019).
ALeRCE broker, the source of the alert detections and non-detections (Forster et al. 2021).
Koji Mukai's list of recent Galactic novae (page updated 2026-10-28), the source of the sample, the positions and the discovery dates.
SNAD mirror of ZTF DR24 light curves, used for the cone downloads.
